scope: Adversarial test of IndiaAI compute-subsidy conditions; bounded Taiwan ADI and Türkiye 1711 comparators. Only the three assigned routes. Retrieval-first and viewpoint-diverse analysis informed by the two requested repositories; no persona testimony, installations, model-score changes, contacts, or signed-pilot claims.

routes.headline: A credible prospective subsidy condition, but stopping the subsidy is not stopping the workload

newEvidence.claim: FACT — E2E's implementation documentation says IndiaAI-SKU services continue running after project expiry at E2E prices; subsidy exhaustion likewise stops the discount, not necessarily the service. This is a documented ordinary-expiry path, not evidence of deliberate safety circumvention.
newEvidence.locator: Billing / Important Consideration; Platform Service final note

newEvidence.claim: FACT — E2E separates subsidised compute/storage from discounted platform services, describes storage upfront charges irrespective of use, and applies overlapping same-SKU projects in first-come order. A project approval value is therefore not a meter reading or government settlement, and an account-level total can misattribute the affected service.
newEvidence.locator: Compute and Storage; Disk and SFS Billing Model Conversion; Multiple IndiaAI Projects Handling

newEvidence.claim: FACT — The linked end-user policy assigns policy updates to IndiaAI and project/subsidy evaluation frameworks to PMEC. It also permits account monitoring and data collection. Its existing access controls and revocability do not specify a model-harm evaluation threshold or adjudication/appeal process.

REPORT — ThePrint's original interviews include Prathosh A.P.'s criticism of affordability, delay and fragmented compute, alongside support for the mission, and a startup applicant reporting a move to AWS. Treat these as attributed experiences, not representative measurements. Its 304-approval snapshot and language of payments must not replace the repository's 303-record allocation audit or a settlement ledger.
newEvidence.locator: ThePrint: 'Not worth it', 'The frontier problem', 'The start-ups'; portal counter; policy §8(f)

newEvidence.claim: FACT — The portal offers a separate early-stage-startup category requiring experience and a senior-official letter, while the regular-startup category lists revenue/funding conditions. Consequently, saying that every startup must satisfy the regular funding threshold would overgeneralise; the alternative route still has a substantive endorsement burden.
newEvidence.locator: Are You Eligible? Startups & MSMEs and Early Stage Startups

newEvidence.claim: RESEARCH RESULT — Qi et al. report that both adversarial and benign fine-tuning can degrade safety alignment in the models they studied. This supports testing the actual post-tuning version rather than relying on a base-model certificate; it does not estimate 2026 Indian deployment risk or the causal effect of a subsidy condition.
newEvidence.locator: Abstract; 2023 study, not a current-model audit

supports: INFERENCE — Existing policy-update and project-evaluation channels make a narrow prospective condition more plausible than an entirely new regulator. The next task is to map the exact test into a current executed provider instrument; a policy power is not itself proof of contractual flow-down.

INFERENCE — Provider SKU/project mechanics make a concrete end-to-end pilot feasible to specify: approval ID, provisioned service, meter, customer invoice, provider claim, government payment and evaluator decision can be joined.
PROPOSAL — A public evaluator subsidy could turn the gate into a useful service for constrained applicants rather than merely another eligibility hurdle. Its funder and usable budget are unresolved.
challenges: INFERENCE — A gate on subsidy payment alone has a documented commercial continuation path. Withholding future public support and suspending a specified service are different remedies and need separately stated authority.

ANALYTICAL LENS, provider — A new model-evaluation duty can entail engineering, dispute and SLA costs beyond ordinary cloud security. No current executed contract establishing acceptance of that duty was retrieved.

ANALYTICAL LENS, applicant/access — Extra approval delay can consume the activation window or impose unused-reservation charges. Independent labs may leave the scheme first, reducing oversight while better-funded users buy ordinary compute. Actual elasticity is unknown.

ANALYTICAL LENS, privacy — Monitoring authority is not proof that raw training data, prompts or model weights need to be centralised. A public/private evaluator may have commercial conflicts even after submitting a declaration.

ANALYTICAL LENS, harm reduction — A submitted report can improve paperwork without changing unsafe behaviour. A base-model pass can be invalidated by fine-tuning; an in-platform hold cannot recall previously exported weights or govern an unrelated offshore deployment.
unknowns: NOT RETRIEVED — Current executed provider agreement, its incorporated security annex and amendments, delegation/signatory record, selected user's award terms, and lawful treatment of sunk reservations.

NOT RETRIEVED — Actual provider subsidy claims, accepted invoices and treasury settlement dates matched to project/SKU metering. Public allocations and press descriptions of money received are not payment evidence.

UNDISCLOSED IN READ SOURCES — Evaluator appointments, compensation/conflict controls, applicant compliance cost, queue-time distribution, appeal outcomes and workload continuation after a safety hold.

INACCESSIBLE — Direct fetches of the original procurement corrigendum, AISI partnership call and AISI FAQ returned HTTP403. Search leads about security-amendment powers and evaluator funding are not admitted as verified findings. No proposition relies on their unexamined detailed answers.
UNSEARCHED IN THIS BOUNDED PASS — A systematic cloud-price/egress comparison, all provider contracts, procurement-law case law and an exhaustive current technical-evaluation literature review.
FUTURE — A pilot outcome before Geneva, 21–22 June 2027, has not occurred at this cutoff.
routes.decisionTest: Before advocating rollout, require one genuinely future award, the operative provider agreement and a written competent-authority decision distinguishing a funding hold from a service hold. Then stage a harmless failed-test fixture and a subsidy-expiry fixture; inspect whether the same model/workload continues under ordinary billing. Reconcile meter, invoice, provider claim and payment separately. If continuation is permitted, describe the route as conditional public support, not a release veto.

ideas.title: Two-switch enforcement and settlement rehearsal
ideas.proposal: Pilot one future IndiaAI project with separately specified subsidy and service-control states. Use a harmless fixture to test failed evaluation, cure, appeal, expiry and conversion to a commercial SKU. Record out-of-platform continuation as a declared scope limit rather than infer compliance from stopped payments.
ideas.owner: Proposed: IndiaAI's authorised policy/procurement owner, one empanelled provider and one consenting future awardee; no party selected or consenting.
ideas.mechanism: Prospective award schedule plus confirmed provider flow-down; reconcile approval ID → SKU → provisioned instance → metered use → customer invoice → accepted subsidy claim → payment date. Address overlapping project precedence explicitly.
ideas.safetyDemand: For one defined model/version, no supported deployment of a pre-agreed critical-failure fixture pending remediation. A service stop is included only if its separate contractual authority is established.
ideas.verification: Witness control-plane state, billing state and inference availability before/after the fixture; record leakage to ordinary billing and previously exported copies. Verify restoration after retest. Report exercised controls separately from real-world harm reduction.
ideas.remedy: Hold the next eligible allocation/subsidy release under signed terms; implement a scoped service hold only if authorised; provide notice, independent review and a retest path. Do not retroactively refuse already valid consumed-service invoices.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: authority/instrument decision by 2027-01-31; rehearsal and settlement follow-up by 2027-05-31; report at 2027-06-21/22.
ideas.whyBetter: Directly tests the newly retrieved commercial-continuation path instead of equating subsidy revocation with an off-switch.

ideas.title: Fund a post-tuning evaluator service, with an access-cost stop rule
ideas.proposal: Provide a small consenting cohort with funded independent post-tuning tests and reusable evidence templates. Pilot in shadow mode before making the test a condition. Compare incremental queue time, applicant staff hours, retest cost, harmful-response failures and benign-task performance to each applicant's baseline; do not presume randomisation or causal identification.
ideas.owner: Proposed: IndiaAI/AISI programme owner with an evaluator not developing the tested model; applicant and provider participation required.
ideas.mechanism: A separately funded evaluation work package and prospective renewal condition, using model hashes and local execution of tests. Selection/conflict disclosures, recusal and second-review rights must precede assignment.
ideas.safetyDemand: Detect and correct safety regression after fine-tuning for a predeclared misuse class, such as assistance with credential-theft fraud, using safe simulated tasks in relevant Indian languages. Do not infer reduced fraud incidents from a benchmark change alone.
ideas.verification: Version-pinned held-out tests, blind second review of disputed results, paired pre/post remediation runs, benign-task false-positive checks, and a minimal signed result artifact. Keep raw private training data local unless separately necessary and authorised.
ideas.remedy: Correction/retest before future supported deployment; abandon or redesign mandatory gating if measured access burden exceeds a pre-agreed cohort tolerance or no reproducible safety improvement appears. The tolerance must be negotiated, not invented here.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: protocol and cost tolerance by 2027-02-28; shadow results and go/no-go by 2027-05-31.
dependencies: Evaluator budget, appointment and conflicts policy
ideas.whyBetter: Tests both substantive safety value and the documented affordability/delay objection; targets changed models rather than rewarding a reusable base-model certificate.

scoreImplications.reason: Policy-update responsibility is explicit, but mapping model-safety obligations to current executed provider terms is unresolved.

scoreImplications.implication: Downside challenge to an off-switch interpretation
scoreImplications.reason: Commercial continuation is documented after ordinary expiry; a safety-triggered stop needs separate authority and engineering.

scoreImplications.implication: Keep allocation reach separate from behavioural reach
scoreImplications.reason: Subsidy/project/SKU accounting and applicant substitution complicate the covered workload denominator.
Approval rules coexist with reported delay, endorsement burdens and user reservation exposure.

scoreImplications.implication: Can be made more specific, not proven higher
scoreImplications.reason: Post-tuning regression is a demonstrated technical failure mode, whereas generic reporting is not harm prevention.

routes.headline: Existing origin restrictions and open-publication incentives require a narrowly scoped post-tuning gate

newEvidence.claim: FACT — The 2026 rules prohibit China-origin/Chinese-funded open models and interfaces such as API/MCP in platform training/inference, and connections to mainland China/Hong Kong/Macao remote IP locations. These are specific existing controls; they do not establish model-harm testing or coverage of work on other clouds.

FACT — Training review rewards willingness to put models and datasets on Hugging Face or GitHub; inference review rewards publishing datasets/code. User content/results remain user-owned, and the platform withdraws access and clears storage after expiry.
newEvidence.locator: §6 review tables, physical pp6–7; §7(2)(2) item1 and §7(2)(3), physical p9

newEvidence.claim: FACT — The privacy consent form describes collecting names, telephone numbers, email addresses and titles for the programme, with purpose/territorial limits. It is not an explicit unrestricted authorisation to disclose training corpora or end-user prompts to a new evaluator.

supports: INFERENCE — Explicit controls and consequences give a prospective appendix a concrete implementation perimeter. A post-tuning release checklist can complement the existing open-publication incentive.
challenges: ANALYTICAL LENS, openness — A blanket no-export or secrecy requirement conflicts with rewarded model sharing; frame a short pre-publication safety check rather than presume all open release is unsafe.

ANALYTICAL LENS, sovereignty versus harm — A provenance restriction can be enforced while an allowed-origin model remains unsafe. Test origin-rule compliance and actual model behaviour as separate outcomes.
INFERENCE — Storage clearing and access withdrawal cannot withdraw user-owned results already downloaded or published. Remedies are strongest before release/expiry and within the platform.
ANALYTICAL LENS, privacy — Reusing three-year logs does not eliminate the need to define evaluator access, redaction and retention for new evidence.
unknowns: NOT RETRIEVED — Operator agreement, prospective 2027 adopted terms/budget and exact amendment delegation. The existing dossier's closed 2026 window is not reopened by these findings.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ RULES — Actual checks of restricted model origin, downloaded/published model inventory, evaluator cost or harm reductions.
UNSEARCHED — Representative Taiwanese SME views and court treatment of these clauses; views above are analytical lenses.
FUTURE — No pre-Geneva safety pilot or adopted 2027 condition is established.
routes.decisionTest: Find one future training award whose applicant intends to publish a tuned model. Confirm that authority/operator/applicant accept a version-linked pre-publication test, its privacy protocol and funding. Demonstrate a hold and retest before publication; record exported versions, rather than claim the platform can revoke public copies.

ideas.title: Safe-publication checkpoint instead of an origin proxy
ideas.proposal: For one genuinely future ADI training cohort, pair the existing open-sharing incentive with a version-linked post-tuning safety result. Record model origin separately from behaviour and release status.
ideas.owner: Proposed: ADI, its appointed future operator, a consenting awardee and an evaluator with declared conflicts.
ideas.mechanism: Prospective award appendix and publication checklist; fund the evaluation within the award plan and require local execution where data are sensitive.
ideas.safetyDemand: Before supported public release, evaluate a declared misuse regression and privacy-leakage test on the final tuned version; fix specified critical findings without a blanket prohibition on open models.
ideas.verification: Model hash, dated test artifact, local synthetic privacy canaries, independent retest and public-release timestamp. Preserve minimal evidence before storage clearing.
ideas.remedy: Hold only authorised remaining support/access before release, with cure and retest; no claim to recall already published weights.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: only if an authorised next-cycle award is available by 2027-03-31, complete release/retest evidence by 2027-05-31; otherwise report the missed decision window.
ideas.whyBetter: Resolves a real tension between open-publication incentives and safety holds, and prevents provenance restrictions being mistaken for demonstrated harmlessness.

scoreImplications.implication: Operational controls strengthened; new-condition authority still qualified
scoreImplications.reason: Detailed use restrictions exist, but do not establish consent to the proposed appendix.
Users own results and can publish; storage deletion is not recall of exported models.

scoreImplications.implication: Require behavioural outcome separate from origin compliance
scoreImplications.reason: Origin restrictions and publication incentives are not safety evaluation results.

routes.headline: Useful conflict-of-interest restrictions, but a funded research partner is not automatically independent assurance

newEvidence.claim: FACT — Programme eligibility excludes related customer/provider entities, companies owned by academics at the participating university from the technology-provider SME role, and declaring university academics as SME employees. These are concrete separation controls, not proof of evaluator independence.

FACT — Call §6.2 says YZE does not claim project intellectual-property rights and is not a party to the participants' output/property agreement; it nevertheless expects data/model/solution sharing with ownership protected. Evaluation access therefore requires an explicit rights-preserving arrangement.

FACT — The website explains that quarterly technical reports go to YZE by the following month-end, with two further weeks for YZE's assessment to TEYDEB. Monitoring cadence alone does not guarantee a reviewed report before 21–22 June 2027.

FACT — The call permits cooperation-agreement signature by project-contract signature, but its earlier IP paragraph and website FAQ still refer to pre-application agreement. This textual inconsistency reinforces the need for a project-specific authorised determination, rather than treating an unsigned agreement as unlimited scope-change permission.
newEvidence.locator: Call §6.2 versus §15.2; FAQ Projenin fikri mülkiyet hakları kime ait olur?

supports: INFERENCE — Existing separation and rights rules give a costed acceptance-test package a more credible starting point than an undefined independent audit.
INFERENCE — An agreed interim deliverable can use the monitoring channel if the review lag is budgeted explicitly.
challenges: ANALYTICAL LENS, evaluator — University and YZE participation combine development/ecosystem and assessment incentives. Formal non-affiliation does not remove dependence on project success or guarantee blinded retesting.

ANALYTICAL LENS, commercial customer — A delayed acceptance can impose costs while a provider has already incurred eligible expenses. Allocate remediation costs and distinguish contractual acceptance from grant eligibility.

FACT/INFERENCE — The FAQ says ordinary project failure does not require repayment, while intentional termination grounds can trigger recovery. A failed safety test must not be silently reclassified as fraud or automatic clawback.
INFERENCE — A domestic customer solution and its acceptance test are a narrower harm pathway than control over upstream frontier-model release.
unknowns: NOT RETRIEVED — One selected but unsigned 2026 award, its permissible scope revisions, current executed cooperation agreement and accepted expense ledger.
UNDISCLOSED — Any separate independent retester, evaluation findings, customer deployment inventory or actual remediation/payment decisions.
UNSEARCHED — Exhaustive Turkish procurement-law interpretation, private consortium objections and actual signature dates.
FUTURE — A 2027 call or Geneva outcome cannot be inferred from annual recurrence.
routes.decisionTest: Identify one eligible project with a still-lawful change window. Obtain a written TÜBİTAK determination reconciling the signature clauses, a ring-fenced test budget and separate acceptance/retest rights. Specify an interim submission date allowing the following-month and YZE review lag before Geneva.

ideas.title: Customer acceptance with a separately appointed retester
ideas.proposal: Add a funded safety acceptance package to one permissible 1711 customer solution, with the development university producing evidence and a non-developing reviewer adjudicating critical disputes.
ideas.owner: Proposed: customer-led consortium and TÜBİTAK/TEYDEB, with YZE's monitoring role and a separate retester defined in writing.
ideas.mechanism: Costed work package, rights-preserving data/test annex, conflict checks and a written customer acceptance condition; keep eligible grant expense and contractual product acceptance separate.
ideas.safetyDemand: Choose one deployment-specific harm before testing—for example unsafe recommendations in an industrial decision-support application—and require critical failure correction before customer production acceptance. Do not apply a generic chatbot refusal test to every project.
ideas.verification: Version-pinned test cases, protected customer data or synthetic fixtures, independent replay of disputed failures, customer acceptance record and an interim report transmitted through the actual monitoring workflow.
ideas.remedy: Customer non-acceptance and correction/retest under agreed terms; any grant withholding or recovery only on independently established programme grounds.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: project/window confirmation by 2027-01-31; evidence package by 2027-04-30, allowing May transmission and early-June review before 2027-06-21/22.
dependencies: All relevant partner rights and signatures
ideas.whyBetter: Uses the actual customer leverage point and report lag, while avoiding the unsupported assumptions that a university partner is independent or that test failure triggers clawback.

scoreImplications.reason: Existing related-party restrictions help, but a non-developing retester adds a real agreement/cost.

scoreImplications.implication: Budget review lag and resolve conflicting signature text
scoreImplications.reason: Quarterly cadence is not a June-ready assessment and the document contains different signature formulations.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not upgrade to automatic safety clawback
scoreImplications.reason: Ordinary failure is distinguished from intentional grounds for recovery; customer acceptance is the more precise proposed lever.
